chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalla', from Ayub ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'Verily, 'Alqamah ibn Muhammad bequeathed to me that I should free a slave on his behalf, so I freed a woman for him. Will that suffice for him, or should I free another from my own wealth?' He said, 'It will suffice for him.' Then he said to me, 'Verily, Fatimah, the mother of my son, bequeathed that I should free a slave on her behalf, so I freed a woman for her.'

key_terms.أَوْصَانِي: He bequeathed to me / He left me a bequest
key_terms.تُجْزِيهِ: Will it suffice him / be accepted on his behalf
key_terms.رَقَبَة: A slave or slave-woman, specifically in the context of manumission (freeing)

ai.seo_question: Is one freed slave sufficient to fulfill a bequest for freeing a slave, or must another be freed from the heir's wealth?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that manumitting a single slave suffices to fulfill a bequest for freeing a slave, clarifying that no additional slave needs to be freed from the heir's personal wealth. He reinforces this legal principle by citing his own practice regarding the bequests of 'Alqamah ibn Muhammad and his daughter Fatimah, demonstrating the consistency of this ruling in the Ahl al-Bayt's tradition.
